summary:
Çorum province stands under the national framework applicable across Türkiye. The sources assembled for this province record no Çorum-specific enforcement actions, incidents or institutions; the findings below are national, and they are what a visitor to Çorum would be subject to.

Human Rights Watch reported on 29 October 2025 that a leaked draft of Türkiye's 11th Judicial Package would amend penal-code article 225 to punish conduct "contrary to biological sex" with up to three years in prison, and would allow charges against anyone taking part in a same-sex engagement or marriage ceremony, carrying up to four years.

The same draft would, under civil-code article 40, raise the minimum age for gender-affirming care from 18 to 25 and impose a permanent-infertility mandate on patients; providers would face fines and up to seven years in prison, and patients up to three years. Fifteen LGBT groups and the Turkish Medical Association objected to the package, and Human Rights Watch called for its withdrawal. Whether the package has since passed is unresolved in the sources.
tangentialFactors:
The draft package sits within a broader pattern of state hostility recorded nationally: the Kaos GL LGBTI+ Human Rights Report 2025 documents 313 violations over the year, dominated by detention decisions, and six deaths linked to anti-LGBTQ violence in 2025, three classified as hate killings, with transgender individuals disproportionately affected.

Çorum's own record in the assembled sources contains no incidents, so the province cannot be distinguished from the national pattern on the evidence available.
localsOnly:
Residents of Çorum face the same national legal exposure as visitors, including the draft provisions on gender-affirming care, which would bind local medical providers with fines and up to seven years' imprisonment and expose patients to up to three years.

Turkey has no comprehensive law prohibiting discrimination on sexual orientation or gender identity, and no direct discrimination protection for gender identity; hormone replacement therapy is not covered by the government healthcare system.
outOfScopeNotes:
Whether the 11th Judicial Package has been enacted since the 29 October 2025 report is unresolved in the sources.

No Çorum-specific enforcement data, detention records or incident reports were present in the inventory; the absence of such records is not evidence of their non-existence.
